invariantAllocations.rationale: Cross-file package and generated-output agreement requires an inventory-driven repository conformance check, package inspection, and isolated generation tests.

invariantAllocations.invariant: External selections, immutable historical evidence, and explicit fixtures are classified separately and are never renumbered as product or owned-contract releases.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Repository-wide semantic classification and prohibited rewrite detection belong to architecture conformance over the exact inventory.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Updated canonical capability definitions remain inert and are never activated from the Program Kit authoring workspace.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Bundle bytes, provider-wrapper rendering, ownership locks, isolated initialization, and authoring-root denial require filesystem conformance tests.

rationale: The existing private Program Kit C# gate is compatible with all Program Kit-owned implementation source in this transition. Version inventories, schema migration, package-byte coordination, bundle refresh, and capability isolation remain explicit executable and architecture conformance obligations; no new analyzer or gate extension is justified.
residualRisks: The selected private gate is a repository-specific policy whose current version itself must be classified and migrated as an owned artifact during the transition.
Static analysis cannot prove repository-wide version intent, exact package contents, migration closure, deterministic replacement schemas, or isolated capability initialization.
nonStaticClaims: Version inventory closure, alpha ordinal mapping, unchanged historical evidence, exact schema registration, migration assessment, package inspection, generated reference agreement, and bundle verification require deterministic executable tests.
Human review remains authoritative for version-intent classification, compatibility disposition, migration acceptance, first stable release policy, and any material scope change.
